title: Biology and biomedicine — Friday, 20 November 2026 arXiv batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a measured popularity list or a survey of bioRxiv, medRxiv, or the medical literature.

sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: The latest available batch is Friday, 20 November 2026; Saturday has no newer batch. Fifteen notable recent papers are highlighted from 40 deduplicated q-bio and medical-physics records. The strongest pattern is computational methods grounded in molecular, genomic, pathology, and clinical-physics data.

sections.title: ShEPhERD-score: Fast, adaptable three-dimensional alignment of molecular features
sections.abstract: A modular differentiable toolkit aligns 3D molecular representations and performs comparably to or better than matched open-source tools in eight of nine DUDE-Z virtual-screening comparisons.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a unified differentiable framework for 3D molecular alignment across shape, electrostatic, and pharmacophore objectives.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is computational virtual screening and alignment performance, not experimental binding or therapeutic activity; the best scoring mode varies by target.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-design fit; benchmarked across protein targets and reports throughput up to 1.03 million alignments per second on one GPU.

sections.title: The Montparnasse Algorithm for RNA Design
sections.abstract: The v2 paper reports a Monte Carlo inverse-folding solver that solved a median 96 of 100 Eterna100 V1 targets over five runs, versus 90 for DesiRNA under the same folding model and budget.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author combines nested rollout search, structural priors, local repair, and parallel workers to improve inverse RNA-folding coverage and speed.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are computational predictions under one secondary-structure energy model; they do not establish that designed RNAs fold as intended in biochemical assays or cells.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct RNA-design relevance; five-run, 100-target benchmark with ViennaRNA 1.8.5 and Turner 1999 model held constant between solvers.

sections.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction
sections.abstract: VenusREM-Harness combines protein-model scores with evolutionary and structural evidence; the v2 paper reports rank-correlation gains across 1,211 assays and 3.1 million measured variants.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a training-free, model-agnostic retrieval-enhanced method that adaptively combines frozen protein-model scores with MSA, structural-confidence, and solvent-exposure information.
sections.unique_caveat: Existing assay benchmarks do not establish performance on newly generated variants or wet-lab outcomes; gains may depend on homolog coverage and benchmark composition.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Retrospective evaluation across ProteinGym, VenusMutHub, and VenusViroHub; reports gains across 71 model configurations.

sections.title: Ab-initio cryo-EM reconstruction from moments of denoised images
sections.abstract: A method-of-moments procedure reconstructs initial 3D cryo-EM models from the first three moments of denoised images, bypassing per-image orientation estimation and initializing refinement on experimental datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report an ab-initio method that avoids explicit particle-orientation estimation and does not assume a uniform orientation distribution.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify denoising-induced bias and loss of fine structure; a low-molecular-weight example fails, making denoising quality a key boundary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct structural-biology method tested on experimental cryo-EM datasets with downstream high-resolution refinement.

sections.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
sections.abstract: HIT-Fuse combines six molecular and pathology modalities across four TCGA cancer cohorts and reports survival stratification, cohort-specific classification gains, and database-based support for some decoded features.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine hierarchical tensor fusion, missing-modality reconstruction, and traceable attributions for integrated genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and digital pathology.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective TCGA evaluation is not independent clinical validation; the authors note no fusion strategy dominates every endpoint, and functional associations do not prove causality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four cancer cohorts and cross-checks against DepMap CRISPR screens, miRTarBase, and protein annotations.

sections.title: OpenTME: An Open Dataset of AI-powered H&E Tumor Microenvironment Profiles from TCGA
sections.abstract: The v2 release describes AI-derived tumor-microenvironment profiles for 5,268 TCGA whole-slide images across ten cancer types, with more than 20,000 quantitative readouts per slide.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors release a dataset of model-generated cell-, tissue-, and spatial-neighborhood readouts from H&E images for computational tumor-microenvironment research.
sections.unique_caveat: The profiles inherit errors from the underlying AI pipeline and are derived from TCGA; the release is for non-commercial academic research and does not constitute validated biomarker measurements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large cancer resource covering ten TCGA cancer types; updated version appeared in the 20 November replacement batch.

sections.title: Morphological Features of Murine Pulmonary Arterial Networks for Diagnosing Vascular Disease
sections.abstract: Geometry, topology, and shape-analysis methods are applied to micro-CT pulmonary arterial networks from 13 mice at four pressures to compare hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension with control morphology.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report morphological differences in hypoxia-induced hypertensive mouse arterial networks and present a feature-extraction and classification pipeline.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a small preclinical mouse study (13 animals), not a validated human diagnostic method; reported discriminative features need independent replication.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Animal micro-CT measurements and multi-pressure assessment; updated version appeared in the 20 November replacement list.

sections.title: First-Passage Time Fluctuation Theorem and Thermodynamic Bound in Cooperative Biomolecular Networks
sections.abstract: A theoretical analysis derives a first-passage-time fluctuation relation and thermodynamic bound for cooperative biomolecular networks, including enzyme- and motor-protein-like systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive a fluctuation theorem for observable first-passage times under stated hidden-current conditions and relate its correction to a bound on kinetic directionality.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is theoretical and conditional on model assumptions; the proposed experimental test is not an experimental validation in this paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct nonequilibrium biomolecular-network relevance; new q-bio replacement version and DOI 10.1021/acs.jpclett.6c02760.

sections.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
sections.abstract: An uncertainty-aware graph method maps genomic-model evidence to distributions over phenotype hypotheses and evaluates association recovery on AlzKB and Hetionet without patient-level phenotype supervision.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors make predictive uncertainty control the breadth of graph-supported phenotype hypotheses while preserving traceable gene-disease-phenotype paths.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational hypothesis generation, not patient-validated variant interpretation; the authors note the gene-holdout advantage is concentrated in three genes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct sequence-to-phenotype application; results include two biomedical graphs and 30 gene-holdout masks against a DistMult baseline.

sections.title: Dynamical Variational Theory of Stochastic Reaction Networks
sections.abstract: A Plefka-expansion variational method approximates non-Markovian reaction-network means, correlations, and responses, with computational benchmarks in gene regulation, enzyme kinetics, and infection dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive a tractable dynamical variational approximation with self-consistent memory and a generalized bubble resummation.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is numerical benchmarking against selected model systems, not direct experimental validation of a biochemical mechanism.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Biochemical and gene-regulatory applications; the paper compares transient and steady-state behavior, including fluctuation-driven effects.

sections.title: GraphEP: A Calibrated Data System and Benchmark for Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology
sections.abstract: GraphEP packages 732 simulated left-ventricular electrophysiology trajectories across 20 anatomies and benchmarks graph-based predictors of transmembrane potential.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that physiology-informed models lead on complementary metrics in this graph-native benchmark.
sections.unique_caveat: The 732 trajectories are mechanistic simulations, not prospective patient data or direct experimental validation of learned predictions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reproducible simulation/data contribution with anatomy, scar, and pacing variation; arXiv comment identifies an AIDaR 2026 NeurIPS workshop paper.

sections.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification
sections.abstract: CALIFUSE uses disagreement among pathology foundation-model representations to estimate confidence and reports calibration and misclassification-detection improvements across seven whole-slide classification tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use encoder-level representational heterogeneity and slide/chunk agreement as confidence cues without training a separate fusion model.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence concerns benchmark classification and calibration; it does not establish clinical deployment or improved patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Seven pathology tasks and comparisons with single-encoder and naive-ensemble baselines; arXiv comment reports acceptance by IEEE BIBM 2026.

sections.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
sections.abstract: A channel-specific hidden Markov model scores seizure-related transition changes in stereo-EEG and is evaluated against medically validated epileptogenic-zone definitions in 30 patients.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that channel-specific latent transition probabilities can improve epileptogenic-zone localization scoring relative to an observation-space baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: One cohort is described; external-site and prospective validation are not reported, so this is not an established clinical decision tool.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomedical signal-analysis question; 30-patient SEEG evaluation compares the method with a benchmark and clinically validated definitions.

sections.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
sections.abstract: An end-to-end reconstruction/inversion model estimates shear-wave speed from undersampled brain MRE data, reports a 30% lower NRMSE than total-variation minimization, and is also applied to in-vivo data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine neural reconstruction with phase-gradient inversion and train the pipeline end-to-end for shear-wave-speed mapping from k-space.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper is an accepted article version, not an independent new validation; image/model error reduction does not establish diagnostic accuracy or patient benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ArXiv comment identifies an accepted IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering version, DOI 10.1109/TBME.2026.3666306; retrospective tests and in-vivo application reported.

sections.title: Towards consensus on practical probabilistic evaluation metrics for clinical decision making in radiotherapy
sections.abstract: The authors apply probabilistic evaluation to 60 proton-therapy plans from three Dutch centers and interview eight radiation oncologists about feasible metrics and probability levels.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors assess probabilistic clinical-goal metrics as a potential complement to current robustness evaluation for radiotherapy planning.
sections.unique_caveat: The study evaluates plans and expert preferences, not prospective decision changes or patient outcomes; validation across more centers is needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Multi-center plan analysis and structured interviews with eight radiation oncologists provide translational evidence beyond a synthetic benchmark.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Molecular design is represented by ShEPhERD-score, Montparnasse, and VenusREM-Harness. Data-driven structural and cancer biology appears in the cryo-EM, HIT-Fuse, and OpenTME papers. Biomolecular dynamics are addressed by a first-passage theorem and a stochastic reaction-network method. These distinct computational, theoretical, and translational studies do not imply a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: Prospectively test molecular-design scores with biochemical assays; stress-test cryo-EM initialization across low-signal and low-molecular-weight targets; evaluate omics and pathology methods on independent cohorts and scanners; extend vascular, electrophysiology, and medical-physics results through external or prospective validation.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The batch is strongest in computational molecular design and structural/genomic methods, with imaging and clinical-physics evaluations also represented. Simulations, model-derived measurements, and retrospective benchmarks dominate; this relevance-ranked snapshot is not a popularity chart or clinical evidence review.
